research.summary: OpenCode CLI静态研究与独立会话审阅；Explicit target proposal, not an upstream fact: build a small Node.js 22, Fastify 5, SQLite, and server-rendered web application in which the Aurora room schedule is the authority. The core is a public busy/free week read model, a transactional half-open-interval claim command, a 409 conflict refusal naming the existing claim and both times, and an owner-or-admin soft cancellation that reopens the window. This is inferred from the web delivery profile and the leaf model of a resource-owned schedule; suite synchronization, approvals, recurrence, and resource administration are deliberately omitted.
research.scope: Check the Aurora room calendar for a free window, claim Thursday 2026-10-22 14:00-16:00, see a clashing claim refused with the conflict named, then cancel and confirm the slot is free again.
unknowns: auxiliary independent static review passed; runtime not_run

The template models one fixed room and one fixed policy; there is no administration console, resource inventory, recurring-series editor, approval flow, delegate routing, notification delivery, or no-show check-in.

Staff identity is delegated to a trusted ingress proxy. The application does not implement SSO, password authentication, CSRF protection for a cookie-based UI, or rate limiting, so it must not be exposed directly to an untrusted network.
The probe verifies the JSON contract and core journey only. It does not install or start the target, render the UI, measure accessibility or performance, or certify security.

The acceptance run requires an isolated disposable SQLite database with the fixed Thursday windows free. The probe exits as not_run with code 2 before any write when setup is unsafe, but it cannot prove that the database is disposable.

Soft-cancelled reservations are retained with no restore, retention, purge, or reporting surface. Changing the room timezone requires a full data review because stored instants are rendered in the configured room zone.
There is no idempotency key. If a 201 response is lost after commit, a retry can be refused as a conflict even though the first claim exists; the operator must inspect the week view.
SQLite is a single-writer authority; the template does not scale horizontally or coordinate multiple writers.

observations.statement: overlaps() parses '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' strings and returns True only when start1 < end2 and start2 < end1, so directly touching intervals are not considered overlapping.

The /bookings POST handler loops over all stored bookings, derives the lab name from each stored description with a regex, and returns HTTP 400 when the lab matches and overlaps(start, end, booking['start'], booking['end']) is true.

delete_event requires an authenticated session, allows admins, otherwise compares the session username with a 'booked by' name parsed from the stored description, and rewrites the rebuilt booking list back to the JSON file.
The embedded FullCalendar initialization uses events:'/bookings', defaults to the month view, sets editable:true, and includes month, agendaWeek, and agendaDay in the header right controls.

The README says the tool is a test tool not intended for serious use without evaluation and modification, identifies file read/write instead of a database as a big disadvantage, and says it may not suit real use cases.

adopted_scope: Week availability read model: GET /api/rooms/aurora/week?weekStart=2026-10-19 returns the Aurora identity, seven local days, confirmed claims as busy blocks, owner-scoped purpose, and 400 INVALID_WEEK_START for a non-Monday week.

Claim submission: POST /api/rooms/aurora/reservations accepts a same-day, 30-minute-aligned, 30-240 minute window inside Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 Asia/Shanghai with a trimmed 1-200 character purpose, stores a confirmed claim, and returns 201.

Conflict refusal: a strict half-open overlap returns 409 SLOT_CONFLICT with the conflicting id plus start/end and a message naming both windows, inserts no row, and leaves touching intervals claimable.

Cancellation and reopening: DELETE /api/rooms/aurora/reservations/:id is owner-or-admin, returns 403 for a non-owner, 204 for a soft cancellation, removes the block from availability, allows a fresh claim, and returns 404 on repeat.
